Class A Receptor Taxonomical Analysis

Kilicali Isildayancan

25 March 2023

Taxonomical Analysis

First look

First we get the TSV file from the UniProt API parser. This file contains names of proteins, their Accession ID, TaxID, Existence, GPCR Domain count, and finally TM count. All is based on UniProt classification.

Domains

Here, we can see that we have 1788 unique proteins with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 14 domain hits. The distribution of the number of domain frequencies are as follows:

TM count

The proteins have a 7+ transmembrane domains with a minimum count of 8 and a maximum of 78 domain hits. The distribution of the number of domain frequencies are as follows:

High-level taxonomy (Superkingdoms, kingdoms, and phylum)

Superkingdoms

  • There are 1 superkingdom(s), namely: Eukaryota. Eukaryotes represent 100% (There are 0 from Bacteria).

Kingdoms

  • There are 1 kingdoms, namely: Metazoa. Here is the distribution:

Phylum

  • There are 13 phylums, namely: Chordata, Arthropoda, Cnidaria, Echinodermata, Annelida, Rotifera, Nematoda, Platyhelminthes, Mollusca, Brachiopoda, Placozoa, Tardigrada, Porifera.

Here is a visual representation of all the phylums present (which covers all the lower-level taxa):

Also the histogram distribution:

The chordates represent 74.4966443 of all the phylums in the reference proteomes with a total of 1332.

Mid-level taxonomy (Order)

We are considering only order here, and looking for primates in particular.

Families of model organisms

Considered model organisms (and respective orders): if they are in our protein phylogeny

  • Mus musculus (Rodentia): TRUE

  • Rattus norvegicus (Rodentia): TRUE

  • Drosophila melanogaster (Drosophilidae): FALSE

  • Bos taurus (Artiodactyla): TRUE

  • Callosobruchus maculatus (Coleoptera): TRUE

  • Danio rerio (Cypriniformes): TRUE

  • Fundulus heteroclitus (Cyprinodontiformes) ~not a “model” : TRUE

  • Nothobranchius furzeri (Cyprinodontiformes): TRUE

  • Oryzias latipes (Beloniformes): TRUE

  • Anolis carolinensis (Squamata): TRUE

  • Gallus gallus (Galliformes): TRUE (UPI001F01E243 is in Gallus gallus?)

  • Taeniopygia castanotis (Passeriformes): TRUE

  • Xenopus laevis (Anura): TRUE

  • Xenopus tropicalis (Anura): TRUE

  • Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Saccharomycetales): FALSE

  • Any primate might be good to start with (Primates): TRUE

  • Caenorhabditis elegans (Rhabditida): TRUE

  • Strongylocentrotus purpuratus (Echinoida): FALSE

There are low amount of hits in Muridae, but it can be interesting since it has Rattus and Mus in it as geni (mice and rats as model organisms)
